The United skipper questioned Carrick’s tactics in that game and argued that the head coach and his staff, rather than the players, were responsible for identifying problems and making changes.
Many outside Old Trafford interpreted the remarks as a challenge to Carrick’s authority, coming only eight days after defender Lisandro Martinez publicly criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s summer recruitment.
Within United, there is said to be sympathy for Fernandes over the situation he found himself in. The Portugal midfielder conducted ten post-match interviews in Como even though he had been replaced by Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half. While some of his comments caused disappointment, the club is understood to accept that his frustration was understandable given the nature of a loss regarded as one of the worst in United’s European history.
It is not yet clear whether Fernandes will be selected for Sunday’s Premier League home match against Bournemouth at Old Trafford. Carrick is due to face questions on the matter when he holds his pre-match news conference on Friday.
Carrick is continuing in charge, although senior United figures are concerned by the team’s performances. Former United striker Wayne Rooney said he watched the Como defeat with shock and disbelief and was as worried about the club’s situation as he has been for a long time.
Rooney, a close friend of Carrick, said he understood why the manager’s decisions were being questioned, but he also described the players as selfish and infantile after the public comments from Martinez and Fernandes.
He said Martinez’s remarks risked splitting the dressing room and predicted that more players could follow with similar criticisms because they were unwilling to take responsibility.
Rooney added that the squad appeared more concerned with their own interests than with their team-mates, the manager, the staff or the supporters, and accused them of complaining and shifting blame elsewhere when things were not going their way.
Fernandes’ form has dropped sharply from last season, when he was named PFA and FWA Player of the Year and set a Premier League record for assists in a single campaign. Rooney suggested Fernandes was directing pressure at others because he did not want to confront his own performances, and said the players needed to look at themselves and show more.
Rooney also urged the United board to clarify Carrick’s future and said Carrick needed to adopt a more combative stance. He said Carrick would be in charge for Sunday’s visit of Bournemouth despite intense speculation that he is close to dismissal after United’s worst run of form since 2015-16.
Reflecting on his own managerial experiences at Plymouth and Birmingham, Rooney said Carrick had to fight for himself because players can drag a manager down and the manager is the one who ends up losing his job.
